IF YOU WANT TO DESIGN LIKE A SENIOR, STOP DRAWING BOXES FIRST.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 QUESTIONS:

How many users, really.

Ten thousand or ten million changes every answer. Demand the number before the diagram.

What breaks first at 10x.

Every design has a weakest link. Name it out loud or the interviewer will.

What you would delete.

Great designs remove parts. If every box is essential, you haven't thought hard enough.

I post daily breakdowns like this for backend, SQL, and interviews.

Follow @owlsky17 so you don't miss the next one.

IF YOU WANT SYSTEMS THAT SURVIVE DAY ONE TRAFFIC, STOP ADDING PARTS.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 RULES:

One database until it screams.

Postgres handles millions of rows before breaking a sweat. Sharding is a last resort, not a design.

Cache one layer at a time.

CDN, then app cache, then query cache. Each layer you skip becomes the outage.

Design the failure first.

What happens when the payment service dies? Answer that before drawing anything else.
